zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 美債回吐多數漲幅，輝達發債吸引$850億訂單

美國與伊朗達成臨時協議，加上製造業數據轉弱，帶動週一美債早盤上漲，但漲勢未能延續至收盤。油價承接上週跌勢，再跌近5%；10年期美債殖利率一度降至4.42%，最後僅下跌1個基點，收在4.47%，30年期則持平於4.97%。投資人歡迎能源供應可望恢復，卻仍難以排除Fed面對的通膨壓力。

協議提高了荷姆茲海峽重新開放的可能性，也降低近期升息的迫切性。交換市場反映的12月前升息1碼機率降至約74%，低於上週一度完全反映升息的水準；直到2027年3月，市場才完整計入1碼升幅。不過，在Kevin Warsh首次以Fed主席身分主持會議前，升息風險仍不低。紐約州製造業明顯放緩，全美製造業產出停滯，但企業回報的成本依然偏高，預期售價還在上升。

企業趁市場氣氛改善取得資金。輝達原擬發行約$200億債券，在收到最高$850億訂單後，將規模提高至$250億。龐大的現金流，加上鮮少進入債市，使這筆交易有別於近期較受關注、槓桿較高的資料中心融資。當天共有8家投資級發行人籌得$360億，科技股也帶動大盤上漲。能源價格下降、企業債需求充裕，卻沒有為最長天期美債帶來多少助益。

## 工廠數據轉弱，尚不足以解除Fed的通膨顧慮

2年期美債殖利率盤中最低來到4.01%，收盤下跌2個基點至4.07%；5年期下跌3個基點至4.18%，表現較佳。2年與10年期利差擴大1個基點至40個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大2個基點至90個基點。5年期相對兩側天期走強，也使2s5s10s蝶式利差下降3個基點至−18個基點；2s10s30s則持平於−10個基點。

從較長區間看，週一延續了既有漲勢。2、5、10及30年期殖利率一週分別下降8、11、9及6個基點，一個月則下降2、8、12及15個基點。最新一日以中期券表現較強，但月度漲幅仍由長端領先。

實質殖利率下降，是當天名目殖利率小幅走低的主要來源。5年期TIPS實質殖利率下跌4個基點至1.78%，7年期下跌2個基點至1.96%，10年期下跌2個基點至2.15%；20及30年期各下跌1個基點，分別至2.52%與2.72%。不過，即使原油大跌，10年期損益兩平通膨率仍上升1個基點至2.32%。

6月紐約州製造業指數由19.6降至5.7，低於市場預估的12.5至14.0。新訂單由22.7降至3.5，出貨由18.9降至8.6，成長動能明顯轉弱。但就業指數從8.3升至9.6，支付價格指數仍高達61.0；供應取得情況惡化，預期售價指數也由43.6升至51.6。訂單成長大幅放緩，並不代表企業成本壓力已經消退。

全美5月工業生產月增0.1%，低於預期的0.2%，4月增幅則修正為0.9%。製造業產出持平，不如預期成長0.3%，產能利用率維持75.7%。其他領域仍有支撐：礦業產出增加1.3%，商業設備增加0.6%，建築用品增加1.1%，整體產能利用率微升至符合預期的76.2%。

這些數據足以支持Fed先觀望，卻還不能確定下一步的方向。本週市場普遍預期利率區間維持3.50%至3.75%，焦點將落在Warsh的預測與首次記者會。當川普總統持續要求降息時，新主席如何回應再度升溫的通膨，格外受到關注。

部分機構預期的緊縮速度，仍遠快於交換市場定價。PGIM撤回4月的降息預測，改估今年升息3次，認為經濟韌性與黏著的通膨要求Fed重建政策可信度；之後才在2027年降息3次、2028年再降1次，將利率帶往3.375%。Citadel Securities也認為，持續的通膨、較強的勞動市場及仍偏高的油價，可能支持最快9月升息。現貨油價下跌減輕了眼前壓力，但尚未改變這些看法，協議中的核議題、制裁與航運條件也仍待釐清。

短期資金利率相對平穩，多數短券殖利率持平。52週國庫券殖利率下跌2個基點至3.84%，與當天近期升息預期降溫的方向一致。

國庫券標售需求則有落差。財政部發行$890.01億91天期國庫券，得標利率3.640%，與前次相同，但投標倍數由2.79降至2.47；間接投標人獲配49.81%，交易商獲配45.42%。$770.00億182天期國庫券得標利率下降1個基點至3.680%，投標倍數大致持平於2.76，間接投標人與交易商分別獲配70.11%及23.33%。兩筆均於6月18日交割。相較於利率的小幅變化，較短天期標售的參與度下降更值得留意。

## 輝達大型發債領銜，信用市場融資需求多元

輝達自2021年以來首度發債，共分7個券次，天期涵蓋2年至30年。最長券次在詢價過程中收斂25個基點，最終利差為美債加65個基點。良好的信用評等、主導性的市場地位，以及本會計年度預計超過$2,000億的自由現金流，支撐了訂單需求；部分資金將用於償還既有債務。高評級債券基金已連續13個月淨流入，也為擴大的發行規模提供了買盤。

其他交易反映出不同的資金用途。KKR支持的Zenobe籌得£9.8億，約合$13億，用於擴充英國與愛爾蘭的電動車及電池車隊。柴油約占車輛全生命週期成本的40%，電動車的電力成本則約占20%；營運節省是投資的重要基礎，但車輛使用率、電價與殘值仍會影響償債能力。

科技公司也透過預付能源債券接觸市政債投資人。美國這類債券今年發行量已超過去年同期的2倍，達$190億；高盛承銷了去年逾40%的交易。公用事業藉此鎖定長期天然氣或電力供應，Alphabet等中介方則以定期付款承諾換取較低成本的融資。投資人實際承擔企業交易對手風險，而合約期限可能遠長於一般公用事業供應契約。

加拿大方面，大蒙特婁REM鐵路系統透過5、7、10及30年期債券籌得C$18.5億。30年期訂單超過該券次規模的5倍，定價殖利率4.791%，較政府債券高95個基點。計畫成本估計C$94億，超支由Caisse承擔。Waste Management of Canada另發行C$7億7年期債券，利差為政府債加72個基點，較初步定價收斂3個基點，為9月到期的C$5億債券預作準備。

槓桿融資的待發行規模也不小，只是多數尚未完成定價。Birkenstock準備睽違5年再度發債，規劃€9億7年期、3年後可贖回債券，用來替換既有債務，並保留增加庫藏股的空間。公司已宣布$2.5億加速股票回購，另表示後續回購可能達$5億。

銀行為EQT可能收購Intertek提出約£50億融資方案，包含歐元與美元槓桿貸款及高收益債。美國銀行則就Ancestry潛在的$22.5億貸款詢問投資人意願，擬再融資2027年到期、合計近$20億債務的一部分；Ancestry另有約$15億高收益債於2028年到期。今年美國貸款發行近80%屬於再融資或重新定價，而2028年將有超過$3,000億槓桿貸款及約$2,500億高收益債到期。即使併購沒有加速，到期債務管理仍足以帶來大量業務。

並非所有借款人的財務狀況都同樣強健。丹麥能源交易商InCommodities因電力與天然氣波動下降，稅前盈餘從€7,250萬降至€290萬，衰退96%，卻仍計畫增加借款。新增債務可以擴大交易能力，但支撐償債的獲利已明顯縮水，這筆融資也尚未完成募集。

歐洲監理機關同時加強檢視銀行與私募信貸的關聯。ECB將審查範圍由約12家銀行擴大至逾20家。德意志銀行、巴克萊、法國巴黎銀行及匯豐合計占歐洲銀行對私募信貸曝險近三分之二，儘管已揭露部位僅約占貸款的2.3%。部分基金近期限制贖回，使這些資金往來更受關注。

德意志銀行預期，戰爭對能源、航運及景氣循環產業的後續影響，將使歐洲利差承受比美國投資級債更大的壓力。其年底預測為：歐元投資級利差擴大近20個基點至95個基點，歐元高收益利差擴大77個基點至345個基點；美元投資級則擴大10個基點至82個基點。該行估計，若總融資成本增加50個基點，歐洲單B級發行人中有44%可能轉為負自由現金流。這些是預測，並非週一實際的利差變動。當天信用ETF表現分歧，LQD微跌0.02%，HYG上漲0.13%，JNK上漲0.16%。

## 歐洲面對產出疲弱，台灣債市受資金緊俏牽制

ECB總裁拉加德表示，能源漲價的間接影響已經出現，因此仍須關注基礎通膨與工資。ECB上週將存款利率升至2.25%，是2023年以來首度升息；貨幣市場仍預期年底前再升1碼至2.5%，並反映25%的機率進一步升至2.75%。

經濟活動卻沒有提供同樣強的緊縮理由。歐元區4月工業生產月增0.1%，低於預期0.2%，也較3月0.4%放緩。資本財產出下降0.5%，能源下降0.4%，中間財增加0.8%，消費財表現較佳。投資疲弱，使ECB必須在成長遲緩與能源衝擊的遞延效果之間權衡。

波蘭央行決策官員Ludwik Kotecki則認為，年底前、甚至2027年3月前都沒有太大理由調整利率。波蘭在2025年5月至今年3月累計降息200個基點後，已連續3個月維持3.75%。5月通膨意外降至3.1%，Kotecki也將取消燃料價格上限可能帶來的反彈視為行政措施效果，而非核心物價重新升溫。他的說法延續了上週波蘭逐漸轉向耐心觀望的政策語氣。

蘇格蘭正準備在2026年第4季或2027年第1季首度公開發債，作為£15億、5年融資計畫的一部分，以增加實質上透過英國政府借款以外的資金來源。承銷商與法律顧問仍在遴選，尚無發行利差。除了流動性與財政能力，投資人也須評估債券到期前蘇格蘭獨立的可能性。

週二亞洲早間有關台灣的報導，凸顯的則是銀行資金不足，而非市場不願承擔風險。季節性繳稅，加上券商為AI股行情大量融資，排擠了銀行可投入公債的資金。5年期殖利率接近2008年以來高點，10年期接近3年高點；銀行為保留流動性減少持有央行定存單，使餘額降至NT$6.15兆，為2010年6月以來最低。近期10年期公債標售殖利率也創2013年以來最高。油價下跌或能減輕通膨疑慮，但眼前壓抑債券需求的，仍是繳稅與貸款成長。

## 新興市場融資環境改善，降息空間仍各不相同

美債殖利率、美元與油價同步走低，有利新興市場資產。EMB上漲0.36%，一週漲幅達1.50%。不過，各國的通膨與融資需求不同，政策選擇也明顯分歧。

巴基斯坦維持基準利率11.5%，符合39位受訪分析師中22位的預期。央行警告，通膨還會在雙位數停留數月，之後才朝5%至7%的中期目標靠攏。5月通膨為11.7%，創2年最快，下一年度經濟成長與通膨預測分別為4%及8.2%。

辛巴威則將利率從35%降至30%，是2024年4月推出ZiG貨幣以來首次降息。總裁John Mushayavanhu將此定位為重新調整，而非寬鬆循環的開始。5月通膨由4.8%降至4.4%，遠低於2025年7月95.8%的高峰；若荷姆茲海峽恢復通行，燃料、肥料與食品成本可望進一步下降。

巴西的調查預測往相反方向變動。經濟學家將2026年底Selic利率預估從13.5%上修至13.75%，2027及2028年的預測也調高。央行已連續2次各降息25個基點至14.5%，但年底通膨預期從5.11%升至5.3%，不僅高於3%目標，也超過4.5%的容忍上限。財政支持與家庭支出仍在支撐需求。

智利的經濟學家與市場定價落差尤其明顯。調查預期11個月內降息25個基點至4.25%，交換市場卻反映一年後利率為4.81%，高出經濟學家預估56個基點。第1季GDP萎縮、失業率升至9.1%，有利未來降息；但核准投資案達創紀錄的$139.6億，以礦業與投資帶動，加上油價仍高於戰前，使交易員保持戒心。

融資計畫則顯示，市場氣氛改善仍須落實為可取得的資金。肯亞打算在2026至2027會計年度發行$11.3億海外債，連同世界銀行與非洲開發銀行的預算支持，將提供近三分之二的外部融資。政府預計借入5,290億先令外債，協助填補相當於GDP 5.5%的赤字。肯亞仍屬債務困境高風險國家，今年2月才透過兩個券次籌得$22.5億。

塞內加爾的Ousmane Sonko軟化了對債務重整的反對立場，表示有可能與IMF達成協議，但仍主張國會應以政府的經濟轉型目標評估各種債務方案。先前發現$70億未揭露借款，使債務超過GDP的130%，IMF也因此暫停$18億融資安排。在油價$115的情境下，燃料補貼可能額外需要約$20億，而原有預算已被突破。公開說法轉趨正面，不代表債務可持續性討論與調整條件已經談妥。

印尼Danantara在近期首度發行5及10年期美元債、籌得$15億後，開始考慮更長天期；該筆規模高於原訂$10億目標。管理層表示，海外投資人對最長30年期債券也有興趣。發行前，公司曾被提醒，印尼市場賣壓可能使借款成本超過6%、甚至達到7%。交易完成與後續市場回穩，促使公司討論延長天期，但尚未敲定30年期發行。

國際金融公司（IFC）則完成另一種新興市場融資：以南美、中東、北非及亞洲的62筆美元貸款為基礎，籌得$5.09億。其中$3.2億優先順位券次暫評Aaa，定價為SOFR加120個基點，較首筆交易的同類券次收斂10個基點。這是IFC第二筆此類交易，透過將民間企業貸款風險移轉給投資人，騰出資本供後續放款。

紐約收盤後，Raizen的重整進一步演變為控制權之爭。IG4 Capital提出收購債權，目標是在債轉股後持有略高於50%的股權。現有方案擬將約650億雷亞爾、約合$128億債務中的45%，轉換為約80%股權。IG4能否達成目標，取決於銀行及公司債持有人是否願意出售。債權人須在接受收購與保留債轉股後持股之間取捨，交易本身尚未完成。

## 科技股大漲、原油下跌，黃金仍獲買盤

S&P 500上漲1.65%，Nasdaq 100上漲3.06%，費城半導體指數大漲5.45%並創新高；VIX下跌8.37%至16.20。科技股領漲，加上輝達龐大的發債訂單，顯示地緣政治緊張緩和後，投資人仍願意為AI成長提供資金。

荷姆茲海峽供應可望恢復，帶動WTI下跌4.87%至$80.75，布蘭特原油下跌4.76%至$83.17，美元指數也下跌0.12%至99.63。對債券投資人而言，這減輕了近期能源與進口物價風險；但美債回吐漲幅，也顯示光靠油價下跌，尚不足以維持早盤的上漲幅度。

黃金期貨在股市上漲、波動率下降之際，仍上漲2.68%至$4,328，顯示保護性需求尚存，但無法單憑價格判定買方在對沖哪一種風險。加上10年期損益兩平通膨率小幅上升，市場仍未把這份協議視為通膨或地緣政治不確定性的終點。

## Warsh首場決策與兩筆長天期標售接續登場

市場預期荷姆茲海峽週五前重新開放，Fed會議也將在此背景下舉行。6月16日美東時間08:30公布進出口物價與住宅數據，17日08:30公布零售銷售，14:00公布FOMC決議，14:30由Warsh召開記者會。維持3.50%至3.75%是市場共識，更重要的是預測與政策說明是否仍為今年稍晚升息留有空間。實際船舶通行與協議文字同樣重要，尤其必須留意再度受阻是否使油價反彈。

6月16日亞洲行程也相當密集。中國將於上海時間10:00公布5月工業生產、零售銷售與固定資產投資；日本央行決議的東京時間尚未確定，市場預期升息25個基點，從約0.75%調至1.00%，後續升息與購債指引將影響日圓及日本公債曲線。澳洲央行於雪梨時間14:30公布決議，預期維持4.35%。

美國財政部16日美東時間11:30標售$650億42天期國庫券，13:00續發$130億、票息5.000%的20年期公債，6月22日交割，2046年5月15日到期。18日13:00另續發$240億、票息1.250%的5年期TIPS，接著19日固定收益市場休市。相較週一國庫券結果，20年期的最終投資人參與度，以及得標殖利率相對發行前交易殖利率的差距，更能直接反映長天期需求；Fed決議後的TIPS標售，則將檢驗投資人對實質殖利率的接受程度。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Treasuries Pare Their Rally as Nvidia Draws $85 Billion of Orders

Treasuries gave back most of an early advance on Monday as investors weighed a US-Iran interim agreement and softer manufacturing data against the inflation pressures still facing the Federal Reserve. Oil fell almost 5%, extending the previous week's retreat, but the 10-year yield finished just 1 basis point lower at 4.47% after touching 4.42%. The 30-year was unchanged at 4.97%.

The agreement strengthened prospects for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and reduced the urgency of a Fed increase. Swaps put the chance of a quarter-point hike by December at about 74%, down from fully priced at one point last week; a full move was not priced until March 2027. That still left considerable tightening risk ahead of Kevin Warsh's first meeting as Fed chair. New York manufacturing slowed sharply, and national manufacturing output was flat, yet firms continued to report elevated costs and higher expected selling prices.

Borrowers took advantage of the improved mood. Nvidia sold $25 billion of bonds, up from an initial target of about $20 billion, after attracting as much as $85 billion of orders. Its cash generation and relative scarcity in the bond market helped distinguish the sale from the more leveraged data-center financing that has occupied credit investors in recent weeks. Eight investment-grade issuers raised $36 billion in total, while technology shares led a broad equity rally. The day brought cheaper energy and ample demand for corporate debt, but little relief for holders of the longest Treasuries.

## Softer Factory Data Leave the Fed's Inflation Problem Unresolved

The 2-year Treasury yield fell 2 basis points to 4.07%, having traded as low as 4.01%, while the 5-year declined 3 basis points to 4.18%. That outperformance widened 2s10s by 1 basis point to 40 and 2s30s by 2 to 90. The 5-year's strength also pulled the 2s5s10s butterfly down 3 basis points to -18; 2s10s30s was unchanged at -10.

Monday extended a rally already visible over the week: 2-, 5-, 10- and 30-year yields were down 8, 11, 9 and 6 basis points, respectively. Over a month, the declines were 2, 8, 12 and 15 basis points. The latest session favored intermediate maturities, even though the long end still led the monthly advance.

Real yields accounted for the day's small nominal gains. The 5-year TIPS yield fell 4 basis points to 1.78%, the 7-year dropped 2 to 1.96%, and the 10-year declined 2 to 2.15%. The 20- and 30-year real yields each eased 1 basis point, to 2.52% and 2.72%. Ten-year inflation compensation nevertheless rose 1 basis point to 2.32%, despite the decline in crude.

The Empire State manufacturing index fell to 5.7 in June from 19.6, below consensus estimates of 12.5 to 14.0. New orders dropped to 3.5 from 22.7 and shipments to 8.6 from 18.9. The weakness was not uniform: employment improved to 9.6 from 8.3, while prices paid remained elevated at 61.0. Supply availability worsened, and expected prices received climbed to 51.6 from 43.6. Factories were reporting much slower growth in orders, not an end to cost pressure.

National industrial production rose 0.1% in May, short of the 0.2% consensus, following a revised 0.9% increase in April. Manufacturing was flat rather than rising the expected 0.3%, with utilization unchanged at 75.7%. Mining output increased 1.3%, business equipment rose 0.6% and construction supplies gained 1.1%. Total capacity utilization edged up to the expected 76.2%.

The combination gives the Fed reason to wait without resolving its next move. This week's decision is widely expected to leave the target range at 3.50%-3.75%. Attention will fall on Warsh's forecasts and first press conference, especially how he addresses renewed inflation while President Donald Trump continues to press for lower rates.

Some investors still see a much faster tightening path than swaps imply. PGIM reversed its April forecast for cuts and now projects three increases this year, arguing that resilient growth and sticky inflation require the Fed to restore credibility. It expects three cuts in 2027 and another in 2028, bringing the rate toward 3.375%. Citadel Securities separately said persistent inflation, stronger labor conditions and still-elevated oil could justify an increase as early as September. The drop in spot crude has reduced the immediate pressure, but it has not erased those views—or settled the agreement's nuclear, sanctions and shipping provisions.

Cash-market rates were comparatively steady, with most short bill yields unchanged. The 52-week yield fell 2 basis points to 3.84%, consistent with the day's reduced expectations for near-term tightening.

Auction demand was less even. Treasury sold $89.001 billion of 91-day bills at 3.640%, unchanged from the previous sale, but bid-to-cover fell to 2.47 from 2.79. Indirect bidders received 49.81% and dealers 45.42%. The $77.000 billion 182-day sale cleared 1 basis point lower at 3.680%, with cover almost unchanged at 2.76, indirect awards of 70.11% and dealers taking 23.33%. Both settle June 18. The weaker participation in the shorter sale stood out more than the small change in auction yields.

## Nvidia's Jumbo Sale Anchors a Busy Credit Market

Nvidia's first bond offering since 2021 comprised seven tranches from 2 to 30 years. The longest tightened 25 basis points during marketing to 65 basis points over Treasuries. Strong ratings, a dominant market position and expected fiscal-year free cash flow above $200 billion supported the order book; proceeds will be used partly to refinance debt. High-grade funds have recorded 13 consecutive months of inflows, giving the market a substantial pool of buyers for the enlarged offering.

The sale came alongside a wide range of financing needs. KKR-backed Zenobe raised £980 million, about $1.3 billion, to expand electric-vehicle and battery fleets in the UK and Ireland. Diesel accounts for roughly 40% of a vehicle's lifetime cost, compared with about 20% for electricity in an EV. Those operating savings underpin the investment case, although utilization, electricity prices and residual values remain important to debt repayment.

Technology companies are also reaching municipal investors through prepaid-energy bonds. US issuance has more than doubled from a year earlier to $19 billion, after Goldman Sachs underwrote more than 40% of last year's transactions. Utilities secure long-term gas or electricity supplies, while intermediaries such as Alphabet obtain cheaper funding in return for scheduled payments. Investors gain corporate counterparty exposure through contracts that can run much longer than a conventional utility supply arrangement.

In Canada, Greater Montreal's REM rail system raised C$1.85 billion across 5-, 7-, 10- and 30-year maturities. Orders for the 30-year exceeded five times the tranche size; it yielded 4.791%, or 95 basis points over government bonds. Project costs are estimated at C$9.4 billion, with the Caisse bearing overruns. Waste Management of Canada sold C$700 million of 7-year notes at 72 basis points over governments, 3 basis points tighter than initial pricing, ahead of a C$500 million maturity in September.

The leveraged pipeline was substantial, though much of it had yet to reach final pricing. Birkenstock was preparing its first bond sale in five years: €900 million of 7-year notes callable after three years, intended to replace existing debt while leaving room for more buybacks. It has announced a $250 million accelerated repurchase and said additional purchases could reach $500 million.

Banks proposed roughly £5 billion of euro- and dollar-denominated loans and high-yield bonds for EQT's possible acquisition of Intertek. Bank of America sounded out investors on a potential $2.25 billion Ancestry loan to refinance part of almost $2 billion due in 2027; the company also has about $1.5 billion of junk bonds maturing in 2028. Nearly 80% of US loan issuance this year has been refinancing or repricing. With more than $300 billion of leveraged loans and about $250 billion of junk bonds due in 2028, maturity management remains a large source of business even without a pickup in acquisitions.

Not all borrowers were approaching lenders from a position of strength. Danish energy trader InCommodities planned to increase borrowing after pretax profit fell 96% to €2.9 million from €72.5 million as power and gas volatility subsided. Additional debt would expand trading capacity just as earnings available to support it had fallen sharply; the financing had not yet been placed.

European credit also faces closer scrutiny of bank exposure to private funds. The ECB expanded its review to more than 20 lenders from about a dozen. Deutsche Bank, Barclays, BNP Paribas and HSBC account for nearly two-thirds of European banks' exposure to private credit, although disclosed positions amount to only about 2.3% of loans. Recent withdrawal limits at some funds have sharpened attention on those links.

Deutsche Bank expects the war's effects on energy, shipping and cyclical companies to weigh more heavily on European spreads than on US investment grade. Its year-end forecasts put euro investment-grade spreads at 95 basis points, almost 20 wider, and euro high yield at 345, up 77. It projects US dollar investment grade at 82, a widening of 10 basis points. Among European single-B issuers, it estimates that 44% could fall into negative free cash flow if total funding costs rose 50 basis points. Those are forecasts rather than Monday's spread changes. Listed credit funds were mixed: LQD edged down 0.02%, while HYG rose 0.13% and JNK gained 0.16%.

## Europe Weighs Weak Output; Taiwan Faces a Cash Squeeze

ECB President Christine Lagarde said the indirect effects of higher energy costs were already appearing, keeping underlying inflation and wages in focus after last week's increase in the deposit rate to 2.25%, the first hike since 2023. Money markets still price another quarter point to 2.5% by year-end, with a 25% chance of a further move to 2.75%.

Activity offers a less hawkish signal. Euro-area industrial production rose 0.1% in April, below the 0.2% consensus and March's 0.4% gain. Capital-goods output fell 0.5% and energy production declined 0.4%; intermediate goods rose 0.8%, and consumer goods performed better. Weak investment leaves the ECB balancing a sluggish economy against the delayed effects of the energy shock.

Polish policymaker Ludwik Kotecki saw little reason to change rates before year-end, and possibly before March 2027. Poland has held at 3.75% for three months after cutting 200 basis points between May 2025 and March. May inflation slowed unexpectedly to 3.1%; Kotecki regarded any rebound from ending the fuel-price cap as an administrative effect rather than renewed core pressure. His comments added to the more patient tone already emerging from Poland last week.

Scotland, meanwhile, was preparing its first public bonds for the fourth quarter of 2026 or first quarter of 2027. The debut forms part of a £1.5 billion, five-year program that would diversify funding beyond borrowing effectively through the UK government. Bookrunner and legal-adviser selection remained under way, with no spread yet established. Investors will have to assess liquidity and fiscal capacity alongside the possibility of independence before the bonds mature.

In Taiwan, reporting early Tuesday described a shortage of bank cash rather than a lack of appetite for risk assets. Seasonal tax payments and heavy brokerage borrowing to finance the AI-led stock rally have reduced funds available for government bonds. Five-year yields were near their highest since 2008 and 10-year yields near a three-year peak. Outstanding central-bank certificates of deposit had fallen to NT$6.15 trillion, the lowest since June 2010, as banks conserved liquidity; recent 10-year auction yields were the highest since 2013. Cheaper oil may ease inflation concerns, but the immediate pressure on bond demand comes from taxes and loan growth.

## Emerging Markets Find Room to Borrow, but Less Room to Ease

Lower Treasury yields, a softer dollar and cheaper oil helped emerging-market assets. EMB rose 0.36%, taking its weekly advance to 1.50%. Domestic inflation and financing needs nevertheless produced markedly different policy decisions.

Pakistan held its benchmark at 11.5%, as expected by 22 of 39 surveyed analysts. The central bank warned that inflation would remain in double digits for several months before moving toward its 5%-7% medium-term target. May inflation was 11.7%, the fastest in two years; next-year growth and inflation were projected at 4% and 8.2%.

Zimbabwe cut to 30% from 35%, its first reduction since introducing the ZiG in April 2024. Governor John Mushayavanhu called it a realignment rather than the beginning of an easing cycle. Inflation had slowed to 4.4% in May from 4.8%, far below its July 2025 peak of 95.8%. Reopening Hormuz could bring further relief through fuel, fertilizer and food costs.

Brazil's survey forecasts moved the other way. Economists raised their end-2026 Selic estimate to 13.75% from 13.5%, and also lifted projections for 2027 and 2028. The central bank has already cut twice by 25 basis points to 14.5%, but expected year-end inflation rose to 5.3% from 5.11%, above both the 3% target and 4.5% upper tolerance. Fiscal support and household spending continue to sustain demand.

Chile showed an unusually large gap between economists and the market. Survey respondents expected a 25-basis-point cut to 4.25% within 11 months, while swaps implied 4.81% in a year, 56 basis points higher than that forecast. First-quarter GDP contracted and unemployment reached 9.1%, supporting the case for eventual easing. Record project approvals worth $13.96 billion, led by mining and investment, and oil still above pre-war levels gave traders reasons to remain cautious.

Borrowing plans underscored how much of the improvement in markets still needs to translate into funding. Kenya plans a $1.13 billion foreign bond in fiscal 2026-27. Along with World Bank and African Development Bank budget support, it would supply nearly two-thirds of external financing. The government expects 529 billion shillings of foreign borrowing to help cover a deficit of 5.5% of GDP. Kenya remains at high risk of debt distress, having already raised $2.25 billion in two tranches in February.

In Senegal, Ousmane Sonko softened his opposition to restructuring and said an IMF agreement was possible, while maintaining that parliament would assess debt solutions against the government's economic-transformation agenda. The discovery of $7 billion of previously undisclosed borrowing pushed debt above 130% of GDP and prompted suspension of a $1.8 billion IMF facility. At oil prices of $115, fuel subsidies could require about $2 billion of extra funding, after the budget had already been exceeded. More constructive public comments did not settle the debt-sustainability discussions or adjustment terms.

Indonesia's Danantara was considering longer maturities after its recent $1.5 billion debut in 5- and 10-year dollar bonds, which exceeded an initial $1 billion goal. Management said international investors had expressed interest in bonds as long as 30 years. Before the sale, it had been warned that the Indonesian selloff might push borrowing costs above 6%, or even to 7%. The completed transaction and subsequent market recovery encouraged discussion of a longer tenor, but no 30-year issue had been agreed.

The International Finance Corp. completed a separate form of emerging-market financing: a $509 million transaction backed by 62 dollar loans across South America, the Middle East, North Africa and Asia. The $320 million senior tranche, provisionally rated Aaa, priced at SOFR plus 120 basis points—10 basis points tighter than its counterpart in the first transaction. This was IFC's second such deal, transferring private-sector loan risk to investors and freeing capital for new lending.

After the New York close, Raizen's restructuring became a contest for control. IG4 Capital offered to buy debt with the aim of owning just over 50% of the company following a proposed conversion of 45% of roughly 65 billion reais, or $12.8 billion, of debt into about 80% of its equity. The plan depended on banks and debenture holders agreeing to sell. Creditors now have to weigh the offer against retaining a stake through the conversion; the acquisition itself was not completed.

## Technology Shares Surge as Oil Falls; Gold Also Gains

The S&P 500 rose 1.65%, the Nasdaq 100 gained 3.06% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped 5.45% to a record. The VIX fell 8.37% to 16.20. Technology's leadership, alongside Nvidia's large order book, showed investors remained willing to finance AI growth as geopolitical tension eased.

WTI dropped 4.87% to $80.75 and Brent fell 4.76% to $83.17 on prospects for renewed supply through Hormuz. The dollar index slipped 0.12% to 99.63. For bond investors, those moves reduced near-term energy and imported-price risks, but the Treasury rally's retracement showed that falling oil alone was not enough to sustain the initial gains.

Gold futures rose 2.68% to $4,328 despite the equity rally and lower volatility. The gain suggested continued demand for protection, although it did not identify which risk buyers were hedging. Together with the small rise in 10-year breakevens, it cautioned against treating the agreement as the end of the inflation or geopolitical uncertainty.

## Warsh's First Decision and Two Long-Duration Auctions Lie Ahead

The Fed meets against expectations that Hormuz will reopen by Friday. Import and export prices and housing data arrive June 16 at 08:30 ET, followed by retail sales June 17 at 08:30. The FOMC decision is due at 14:00, with Warsh's press conference at 14:30. A hold at 3.50%-3.75% is the consensus; the larger question is whether the forecasts and guidance leave room for a hike later this year. Actual shipping flows will matter as much as the agreement's wording, particularly if renewed obstruction reverses the oil decline.

Asia has its own dense calendar on June 16. China releases May industrial production, retail sales and fixed-asset investment at 10:00 Shanghai time. The Bank of Japan's decision, at an unspecified Tokyo time, is expected to lift the policy rate 25 basis points from about 0.75% to 1.00%; its guidance on further increases and bond purchases will be important for the yen and JGB curve. The Reserve Bank of Australia announces at 14:30 Sydney time, with a hold at 4.35% expected.

Treasury sells $65 billion of 42-day bills June 16 at 11:30 ET, followed at 13:00 by a $13 billion reopening of the 5.000% 20-year bond. The bond settles June 22 and matures May 15, 2046. A $24 billion reopening of the 1.250% 5-year TIPS follows June 18 at 13:00, before the June 19 fixed-income holiday. End-user participation and the 20-year stop relative to its when-issued yield will offer a more direct reading of demand for duration than Monday's bill results. The TIPS sale will then test real-yield demand immediately after the Fed decision.

overall_summary.headline: Treasury rally fades as Nvidia's $25 billion sale draws heavy demand
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries initially rallied as the US-Iran interim agreement raised hopes of reopening Hormuz. The 2-year yield touched 4.01% before closing at 4.07%, down 2 basis points; the 10-year retraced from 4.42% to 4.47%, down just 1. The 30-year was unchanged at 4.97%. Ten-year real yields fell 2 basis points to 2.15%, but inflation compensation rose 1 to 2.32%.

New York manufacturing slowed sharply, and national manufacturing output was flat. Costs and expected selling prices remained elevated, however, leaving a substantial chance of further Fed tightening: swaps priced about 74% odds of a quarter-point increase by December. Warsh's first decision is expected to leave the 3.50%-3.75% range unchanged; his forecasts and guidance will draw closer scrutiny.

Nvidia attracted as much as $85 billion of orders for an upsized $25 billion offering, helping eight investment-grade borrowers raise $36 billion. Its cash generation supported strong execution even as European lenders faced closer scrutiny of private-credit exposure. Overseas, Lagarde emphasized lingering energy effects, while Taiwan's tax payments and AI-related borrowing squeezed bank liquidity. Lower oil improved the backdrop without removing those local constraints.
overall_summary.summary: The US-Iran interim agreement sent oil almost 5% lower, but the 10-year yield finished just 1 basis point lower at 4.47%. Softer manufacturing data left inflation concerns unresolved ahead of Warsh's first Fed meeting.
